title.narrative: Kvinna till Kvinna EU accession and Women´s Rights Western Balkans 2020-2026
Kvinna till Kvinna EU-närmande och kvinnors rättigheter Västra Balkan 2020-2026

description.narrative:
Intended impact:
Womens rights are increasingly respected and equal participation in decision-making takes place in the Western Balkans
Programme outcomes:
1. Kvinna till Kvinna and Women's Civil Society Organisations (WCSOs) have strengthened engagement on gender equality with European Union (EU), member states, United Nations (UN), and other national stakeholders
2. Kvinna till Kvinna and targeted WCSOs have built new alliances and strengthened existing ones to promote gender equality in Western Balkans.
3. Targeted WCSOs have the capacity to conduct effective advocacy.
Assumptions:
Western Balkan Governments and parliaments • continue to be committed to the EU accession processes; • realise the necessity to promote, respect and implement laws and policies relevant for womens rights and womens participation and influence, and to persecute any violations of such legislation; • commit to upholding the rule of law.
EU and other international stakeholders • uphold their own commitments andde clared principles regarding realising gender equality and protecting womensrights and womens participation; • uphold their own commitments and declared principles regarding priorities in the pre-accession process of the Western Balkan countries; and • insist on adherence/fulfilment of the requirements of the acquis.

Programmet syftar till att stärka kvinnors rättigheter och lika deltagande i beslutsfattande i västra Balkan, att bidra till att integrera jämställdhet i EU-närmandeprocessen samt att stärka kvinnorättsrörelsen i de sex förmedlemskapsländerna. Programmet fokuserar på påverkansarbete gentemot EU:s institutioner. Förändringsteorin går ut på att om EU lever upp till sina åtaganden om mänskliga rättigheter och jämställdhet kommer det att påverka regeringar och parlament i västra Balkan-regionen så att de stiftar och genomför lagar och policys som är relevanta för kvinnors rättigheter och lika deltagande. Programmet stödjer femton lokala organisaitoner i regionen som tillsammans bedriver påverkansarbete både på nationell nivå och på EU-nivå.

The program aims to continue to strengthen women's rights and women's equal participation in decision-making in the Western Balkan region, and to contribute to gendering the EU accession processes and strengthening civil society organisations the six pre-accession countries. Focus in the program implementation is put on advocacy towards EU institutions. The theory of change is that if EU upholds its commitments to human rights and gender equality it will have a direct influence on the Western Balkan governments and parliaments to legislate for and implement laws and policies relevant for women’s rights and women’s equal participation. The program provides financial support and capacity building to 15 strategic partner organisations in the region to join and effectively influence policy discussions at national level, at the EU level and in other international fora.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement, Sida-Kvinna till Kvinna , EU Accession and Womens Rights Western Balkans
Beslut om insats, Kvinna till Kvinna EU Accession and Womens Rights Western Balkans

description.narrative:
Outcome 1 (engagement with stakeholders)
The program has strengthened partners' engagement on gender equality with the EU and other stakeholders and has contributed to put gender equality in the EU-accession process higher on the agenda in Brussels.
Kvinna till Kvinna and the partners in the program have increasingly been recognized as the experts, information sources, and the ones to turn to regarding gender equality in the Western Balkans. This is a result of advocacy and relationship-building as well as published research, analyses and reports. Kvinna till Kvinna and partners have been invited to various events and meetings, requested to present publications, and asked for input in different processes such as the enlargement process and the EU GAP III process. The program has initiated a Women's Civil Society Sounding Board for the EU Delegation to Serbia, as a platform for information sharing and advocacy.
The program was also involved in the Berlin Process. Previous advocacy through this and another regional EU-advocacy program, contributed to that gender equality was prioritised as a high-level dialogue at the regional agenda.
The Brussels-based advocacy was complemented by different coordinated actions across the region as well as at the national level led by the local partners. Women's CSOs deepened their engagement with EU and other institutional stakeholders, enabling them to push for gender-responsive policies and highlight gendered impact of current legislation and reforms. Several organisations managed to directly influence strategic documents such as the EC Country Reports, action plans for Roma inclusion, and green transition strategies, showing a clear link between their advocacy and policy uptake.
Outcome 2 (alliances)
The program played a catalytic role in creating new alliances, such as around the Serbia-Kosovo dialogue where new partners joined, broadening the discussion to exchange information and strategies on the anti-gender movement in the two countries. Other collaborations and alliances around strategies towards the anti-gender movement and the WPS agenda respectively have also been created among partners and others. The work of these alliances have been facilitated and strengthened through the Advocacy Hub (digital platform) created through the program.
Outcome 3 (capacity)
Partners in the program are highly capacitated, and/but the program has managed to further build capacity among partners. There is improved advocacy skills, enhanced message clarity, strengthened confidence among partners, and that partners have gone through transformational growth and strengthened in their role as advocates for gender equality. Kvinna till Kvinna has been a mentor and facilitator in partners' advocacy and other work, enabling them to get quick information about events and contacts in the EU institutions. There are several examples of partners taking on leadership roles within coalitions, steering collective advocacy campaigns, and producing harmonised policy recommendations.
